question: S. 4668, as amended
plain_language: The Senate passed the college-sports bill as rewritten into the Protect College Sports Act, covering athlete publicity rights, agents, medical coverage, transfers, and college-sports broadcasts. A Yea passes that bill. A Nay votes no.

question: Booker Amdt. No. 6835
plain_language: This amendment would have let coaches move between four-year colleges under transfer rules like those for athletes, and it would have voided a coach's endorsement deal unless the pay matched similar non-coaches and had a real business purpose. A Yea would have added those rules. A Nay rejected them.

question: Booker Amdt. No. 6805
plain_language: This amendment would have capped a student-athlete insurance and catastrophic-injury fund at $200 million and required major conferences and an athletic association to cover any amount above $100 million. A Yea would have set that cap. A Nay rejected it.

question: Kennedy Amdt. No. 6760
plain_language: This amendment would have barred colleges, conferences, and athletic associations from raising ticket prices for a sport by more than 4 percent from the prior academic year. A Yea would have added that cap. A Nay rejected it.

question: Paul Amdt. No. 6758
plain_language: This amendment would have replaced the college-sports bill with the Collegiate Sports Integrity Act, which centers on an antitrust exemption for athletic conferences and associations. A Yea would have made that swap. A Nay rejected it.

question: Baldwin Amdt. No. 6828
plain_language: This amendment rewrites the college-sports bill's preemption section so states generally cannot set conflicting rules on athlete publicity pay, transfers, or certain eligibility, while keeping state civil-rights, contract, privacy, and similar laws unless they conflict. A Yea adopts that text. A Nay rejects it.

question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: S. 4668, as Amended
result: Cloture Motion Agreed to (74-25, 3/5 majority required)
plain_language: This vote would end debate on the college-sports bill after it was rewritten as the Protect College Sports Act. A Yea limits debate so the Senate can move to a final passage vote. A Nay keeps debate open.

question: Amdt. No. 6776
plain_language: This substitute rewrites the college-sports bill as the Protect College Sports Act, covering athlete publicity rights, agents, medical coverage, transfers, and college-sports broadcasts. A Yea adopts that rewrite. A Nay would have left the earlier text.

question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Cruz Amdt. No. 6776
result: Cloture Motion Agreed to (70-21, 3/5 majority required)
plain_language: This vote would end debate on a substitute that rewrites the college-sports bill as the Protect College Sports Act, covering athlete publicity rights, agents, medical coverage, transfers, and college-sports broadcasts. A Yea limits debate on that rewrite. A Nay keeps debate open.

question: Motion to Proceed to S. 4668
plain_language: This vote starts formal consideration of the college-sports bill on athletes' name, image, and likeness rights, agents, and transfers. A Yea takes up the bill. A Nay refuses to take it up.

question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to S. 4668
result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to (74-24, 3/5 majority required)
plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on taking up a college-sports bill on athletes' name, image, and likeness rights, agents, transfers, and a limited antitrust exemption for selling some media rights. A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up the bill. A Nay would have blocked ending debate.
